AgentConfig.description:
The full, admin-editable configuration of one agent (stored as JSON).

``v`` accepts ``1`` for one release: v1 rows are rewritten to v2 by the
``v2_008_agentconfig_v2`` migration, and the console still posts ``v: 1``
until WP-3 lands.

default.safe_reply: I'm sorry, I can't help with that. Is there anything else I can help you with?

tests.description: Simulated conversations the agent is tested with (V5-29); they version with the config.
tests.title: Tests

timezone.description: The business timezone (IANA name): opening hours and bookings are in this zone.
timezone.title: Timezone

default.greeting: Hello! How can I help you today?

AgentConfig.title: AgentConfig

AgentNode.description: One conversational step with its own instructions, tools and extractions.
AgentNode.title: AgentNode

AgentTest.description: One simulated conversation: who the caller is, what they want, what must happen.

expectations.description: What must be true of the agent's side, one statement each (the accuracy and task-completion judges check them).
expectations.title: Expectations

id.description: Stable case id, unique in the agent.
id.title: Id

max_turns.description: Caller turns before the conversation is stopped.
max_turns.title: Max Turns

mocks.description: Tool name → the result the tool returns in this case instead of calling out (HTTP tools and connected-app actions). A string is returned as-is; anything else as JSON.
mocks.title: Mocks

persona_instructions.description: Who the simulated caller is and how they talk (played by an LLM).
persona_instructions.title: Persona Instructions

scenario.description: What the caller wants in this conversation; the persona pursues it.

AmdConfig.description:
Answering-machine detection on outbound calls (``TelephonyConfig.amd``, V5-32).

When ``enabled``, the worker listens to how an outbound call is answered and
classifies it with the agent's own speech-to-text and language model before
the agent speaks. A person (or an unsure result) → the conversation goes on as
usual. A voicemail greeting → ``on_machine``: ``leave_message`` speaks
``message`` after the greeting and hangs up; ``hangup`` hangs up at once. A
mailbox that cannot take a message is always hung up. A phone menu is
navigated by the agent when ``ivr_detection`` is on, else treated as a machine.
Inbound calls and web sessions ignore this setting.

ivr_detection.description: Let the agent navigate a phone menu instead of hanging up on it.
ivr_detection.title: Ivr Detection

message.description: What the agent says to a voicemail (leave_message). Empty: a short call-back request.
message.title: Message

AmdConfig.title: AmdConfig

``AgentConfig.tools.apps``: how the agent uses connected apps (docs/v5/COMPOSIO.md D-V5-C6).

The default ``off`` changes nothing for an agent saved before this field existed.

accounts.description: Per app (toolkit slug), the accounts (connection ids) the app server or tool finder may use (R-V5-13); an app not named, or named with an empty list, uses its default account. At most 20 apps and 5 accounts per app
accounts.title: Accounts

allowed_toolkits.description: Apps the app server or tool finder may use (toolkit slugs); empty = every connected app of the agent
allowed_toolkits.title: Allowed Toolkits

denied_actions.description: Actions the app server or tool finder must never run (action slugs)
denied_actions.title: Denied Actions

reviewed_actions.description: Destructive actions the builder has decided about (action slugs, R-V5-9); denied_actions says which way. An unreviewed destructive action is blocked
reviewed_actions.title: Reviewed Actions

AppsMode.title: AppsMode

AppsRouterOptions.description: What the tool finder may do (D-V5-C7).

execute.description: Let the agent run the actions it found
execute.title: Execute

manage_connections.description: Let the agent offer a sign-in link for an app that is not connected yet (text and web chats only: a phone caller cannot open a link)
manage_connections.title: Manage Connections

search.description: Let the agent look actions up during the conversation
search.title: Search

ChecklistSetItemAction.title: ChecklistSetItemAction

What a probed LiveKit deployment supports (CONTRACTS-V2 §4.3).

Defaults describe the most restrictive target (a bare self-hosted server), so
an unprobed connection never advertises a feature it may not have.
ConnectionCapabilities.title: ConnectionCapabilities

ConnectionInfo.title: ConnectionInfo

DatasetToolDefinition.description:
A lookup in one of the workspace's datasets (V6-16, D-V6-27; ``lkap_contracts.datasets``).

The model sees one string argument per key column (``key_columns``, minus the pinned
ones) and gets back at most ``max_rows`` rows with ``return_columns`` (all columns when
empty), matched ``exact`` or by ``prefix`` on the normalised value. The worker calls the
api's internal lookup route with the session, so a lookup never reads another
workspace's dataset, and fences the rows as ``dataset:<name>``. Read-only: nothing is
ever written to a dataset from a call. The tool always runs blocking (a lookup is quick).

V6-07: ``pinned_arguments`` fix a key column's value, hidden from the model (a string may
be ``{{ ctx.caller_phone }}`` or ``{{ var.policy_number }}``); ``requires_vars`` refuse
until variables are set; ``bindings`` copy a successful lookup onto the panel. The bound
(and model-visible) result is the list of rows, so ``/0/holder_name`` is the first row's
``holder_name``.
DatasetToolDefinition.title: DatasetToolDefinition

DetailsSetAction.description: Write one row of a ``details`` block (``value`` may name ``{{ var.<name> }}``).
DetailsSetAction.title: DetailsSetAction

DisclosureConfig.description:
Telling callers they are talking to an AI (V5-15, D-V5-22): on by default.

``greeting`` puts the line at the start of the spoken greeting (a
``{disclosure}`` placeholder in the greeting marks where, otherwise it goes
first); ``banner`` leaves it to the on-screen banner of a ``consent`` block;
``both`` does both. On a phone call there is no screen, so ``banner`` is
spoken in the greeting too.

text.description: The disclosure line; empty uses the workspace's (Settings → Compliance).
text.title: Text

DisclosureConfig.title: DisclosureConfig

DispositionSetAction.description: Set the session's outcome label (a flow's ``disposition``).
DispositionSetAction.title: DispositionSetAction

EndNode.description: Terminal node: says farewell, records a disposition and ends the session.
EndNode.title: EndNode

EndpointingOptions.description: When the caller's turn counts as finished (SDK ``EndpointingOptions``, ``turn.py:113``).
EndpointingOptions.title: EndpointingOptions

EscalateAction.description: Flag the session for a person, as ``escalate_to_human`` does, with the rule's reason.
EscalateAction.title: EscalateAction

EveryNTurnsTrigger.description: After every ``n``-th caller turn (``n = 1``: every turn).
EveryNTurnsTrigger.title: EveryNTurnsTrigger

ExtractionConfig.description: What the agent captures from the conversation while it talks (off by default).
ExtractionConfig.title: ExtractionConfig

ExtractionField.description: One fact to capture: a flow ``VariableSpec`` plus how to ask for it and where it shows.
ExtractionField.title: ExtractionField

FlowEdge.description: A conditional transition; ``condition`` becomes the handoff tool description.
FlowEdge.title: FlowEdge

FlowSpec.description: The whole graph, validated structurally on construction.
FlowSpec.title: FlowSpec

GlobalNode.description: Instructions, tools and knowledge merged into every agent node.
GlobalNode.title: GlobalNode

GuardrailsConfig.description: What the agent checks, and what it does when a check trips (V5-39). Empty by default: no checks.

budget_ms.description: How long a classifier or moderation check may take; past it the text goes through and a `guardrail_timeout` event is recorded.
budget_ms.title: Budget Ms

input.description: Rules on what the caller says (each finished turn).
input.title: Input

model.description: The language model that judges classifier rules (a small, fast one is best); `None` uses the agent's workflow model.

on_trip.description: What a trip on what the caller or the agent says does: `interrupt` stops the agent and says the safe reply; `end_call` also ends the call; `escalate` also asks a person to take over (`escalate_to_human`). A tool's result that trips is always replaced by the safe reply.
on_trip.title: On Trip

output.description: Rules on what the agent says, checked one sentence at a time as it speaks.
output.title: Output

safe_reply.default: I'm sorry, I can't help with that. Is there anything else I can help you with?
safe_reply.description: What the agent says after a trip, word for word.
safe_reply.title: Safe Reply

tool_output.description: Rules on what a tool returns, checked before the agent reads it.
tool_output.title: Tool Output

GuardrailsConfig.title: GuardrailsConfig

HttpToolDefinition.description: An HTTP call exposed to the model as a raw-schema function tool.
HttpToolDefinition.title: HttpToolDefinition

InstructAction.description: A system note for the model's next reply only (sent as written; no placeholders).
InstructAction.title: InstructAction

InterruptionOptions.description: How the caller interrupts the agent (SDK ``InterruptionOptions``, ``turn.py:150``).
InterruptionOptions.title: InterruptionOptions

KnowledgeConfig.description:
Knowledge bases attached to the agent and how they are injected.

The v2 fields (V5-06) default so an agent saved before them retrieves at
least what it did: hybrid search on, no score floor, no rerank.

max_inject_tokens.description: Upper bound on the knowledge note added to a turn (approximate tokens).
max_inject_tokens.title: Max Inject Tokens

min_score.description: Drop hits scoring below this (0-1); null keeps every hit. In hybrid mode without rerank the score is rank-derived, so a floor only trims the tail of the list.
min_score.title: Min Score

mode.description: `hybrid` fuses keyword matches with embedding similarity.
mode.title: Mode

prefetch.description: Start the auto-inject search on the caller's interim transcript, so the result is usually ready when the turn ends.
prefetch.title: Prefetch

query_mode.description: `conversation` searches with the last user turn plus the previous assistant sentence and flow variables; `last_turn` with the user's words only.
query_mode.title: Query Mode

rerank.description: `local` rescores the candidates with the local cross-encoder (adds ~60-100 ms).
rerank.title: Rerank

skip_short_turns.description: Skip the auto-inject search for backchannels and very short turns (yes, okay, digits).
skip_short_turns.title: Skip Short Turns

KnowledgeConfig.title: KnowledgeConfig

LocaleConfig.description:
Whose clock the agent talks in (R-V5-10).

``AgentConfig.timezone`` stays the **business** timezone (opening hours, seeds,
booking defaults); this block says how the **caller's** timezone is chosen at
session start.

caller_timezone.description: `detect` uses the caller's own timezone (from the browser, else the phone number, else the business timezone); `business` always uses the business timezone.
caller_timezone.title: Caller Timezone

LocaleConfig.title: LocaleConfig

ManualTrigger.description: The agent gets the ``extract_now`` tool and decides when to run it.
ManualTrigger.title: ManualTrigger

McpHeaderAuth.description:
Static request headers, typically an API key (research-v4 tools §4.3.1).

Header values may reference ``{{ secret.NAME }}``; the api substitutes them from
``credential_id`` (an ``http-tool-secret`` bag) when a session resolves.
McpHeaderAuth.title: McpHeaderAuth

McpNoAuth.description: The MCP server needs no credentials (a public server).
McpNoAuth.title: McpNoAuth

McpOAuthAccess.description:
V5-16: one signed-in MCP server's short-lived access, as the worker receives it.

The api is the OAuth client (research-v4 tools §4.3.6): it keeps the refresh token,
the client secret and the token endpoint, and hands the worker only an access token
that expires minutes from now. ``name`` and ``url`` match the server's entry in
:attr:`ResolvedAgentConfig.tools`; ``tool_id`` is what the worker names when it asks
``POST /internal/v1/tools/{tool_id}/oauth/token`` for a fresh token. ``access_token``
is ``None`` when the api could not refresh it at session start (the worker fetches one
before its first request). **Contains a secret.**
McpOAuthAccess.title: McpOAuthAccess

McpOAuthAuth.description:
Sign in through the server's OAuth provider (V5-14; saved only once V5-14 lands).

The api is the OAuth client: it runs discovery, registration, consent and the token
exchange, keeps the tokens in an ``mcp-oauth`` credential, and hands the worker a
short-lived access token at session start (research-v4 tools §4.3).
McpOAuthAuth.title: McpOAuthAuth

McpServerDefinition.description:
A streamable-HTTP MCP server attached to the agent.

``auth`` says how the worker authenticates. ``headers`` and ``credential_id`` are the
pre-V5-09 shape, kept as **deprecated mirrors** of header auth so readers that have not
moved to ``auth`` yet keep working: a definition that sets them without ``auth`` (or
with ``auth.kind == "none"``) folds them into :class:`McpHeaderAuth`; with ``auth`` set
they are filled from it (``credential_id`` also mirrors an OAuth credential), and a
value that disagrees with ``auth`` is an error. Stored rows need no data migration:
they load as header auth and re-save with ``auth``.
McpServerDefinition.title: McpServerDefinition

McpServerOrigin.description: Where a provider-provisioned MCP server comes from (docs/v5/COMPOSIO.md §3).
McpServerOrigin.title: McpServerOrigin

McpToolSnapshot.description: One tool of a server's ``tools/list`` answer, as ``POST /v1/tools/{id}/test`` stored it.
McpToolSnapshot.title: McpToolSnapshot

MemoryConfig.description:
What the agent remembers about a returning caller (V5-40, D-V5-17). Off by default.

Callers are identified by a pseudonymous id (a keyed hash of their phone number or of
the identity the embedding site passed), never by the number itself. The memories are
read once when the session starts and written once after it ends, never during the call.

consent_line.description: A sentence the agent says early in the call when the session will be remembered (for example that the conversation is remembered to help next time). `None`: no line.
consent_line.title: Consent Line

enabled.description: Remember callers across sessions. Nothing is read or written while this is off.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_recall_tokens.description: The most text (in tokens, about four characters each) of recalled memories added to the agent's instructions at the start of a session.
max_recall_tokens.title: Max Recall Tokens

retention_days.description: Days a caller's memories are kept after their last session; then they are deleted.
retention_days.title: Retention Days

scope.description: `agent`: only this agent reads and writes its memories of a caller; `workspace`: the memories are shared with every agent of the workspace that also uses `workspace`.
scope.title: Scope

verbatim.description: Store what the caller said as it was, without a model picking out the facts (no model call; the masking of `privacy.storage_tier` still applies). Off: the agent's language model extracts short facts after the call.
verbatim.title: Verbatim

MemoryConfig.title: MemoryConfig

ModelCapabilities.description:
What one model can do, as far as the platform knows (D-V4-24, R-V4-23).

``None`` means unknown. Resolved per field from, in order: the admin's
declaration, the last "Test model" probe, the live catalog item's
metadata, the registry; ``source`` names the source of ``vision``.
ModelCapabilities.title: ModelCapabilities

NodeExitTrigger.description: When a flow leaves one of these steps (empty: any step).
NodeExitTrigger.title: NodeExitTrigger

NotePushAction.description: Push a note (``text`` may name ``{{ var.<name> }}``); in ``block_id``'s margin when given.
NotePushAction.title: NotePushAction

NotifyTeamConfig.description:
Where ``notify_team`` (and ``escalate_to_human``) posts a summary for the team (V5-25).

The webhook URL is a secret: it is kept in an ``http-tool-secret`` key under
``secret_name`` and reaches the worker resolved, never in the stored config.

credential_id.description: An `http-tool-secret` key holding the webhook URL
credential_id.title: Credential Id

include_transcript.description: Add the recent conversation to the message. Off by default: a transcript may hold personal details.
include_transcript.title: Include Transcript

on_escalation.description: Also post when the agent escalates the call to a person
on_escalation.title: On Escalation

secret_name.description: The name the webhook URL is stored under in that key
secret_name.title: Secret Name

style.description: `slack` posts a Slack message; `generic` posts JSON fields
style.title: Style

NotifyTeamConfig.title: NotifyTeamConfig

PanelLayout.description: Which panel renders the session, and (for ``composite``) its blocks.

accept_state_delta.description: Let the caller's page change what some panel blocks show (V5-43, ruling on ask #309). On, the page may send an AG-UI `STATE_DELTA` (`AgentAction.action == "state_delta"`) that writes the display blocks `update_block` may write, except `kb_citations` and `custom`; requestable, link, consent, upload, captions and handoff blocks are never writable from the page. Off (the default), every such change is refused, so the page cannot alter what `describe_panel` hands the model or what the console's live view shows.
accept_state_delta.title: Accept State Delta

PanelLayout.title: PanelLayout

PipelineConfig.description:
Which providers fill which slot, and how turns are handled.

Slot requirements per mode are reported by :func:`pipeline_issues` rather
than raised here: the api returns them as a ``ValidationResult`` so a
half-finished pipeline can still be saved as a draft.
PipelineConfig.title: PipelineConfig

PreemptiveGenerationOptions.description: Start the reply before the caller's turn is confirmed (SDK ``turn.py:201``).
PreemptiveGenerationOptions.title: PreemptiveGenerationOptions

PrivacyConfig.description:
What the platform keeps and shares about a caller (V5-30, P §4.2 C10).

The defaults keep today's behaviour: nothing is masked, every session is
kept in full and third-party telemetry receives the conversation.

scrub_model.description: An LLM that also masks names, addresses and other personal details after the call when `storage_tier` is not `full`. Only an OpenAI-compatible provider with a key (OpenAI, OpenRouter) can run from the api; others are skipped with a warning.

storage_tier.description: What is kept after the call: `full` everything; `redacted` the transcript and events with card numbers, emails, phone numbers and long numbers masked (and the `scrub_model` pass when set); `basic` also drops tool arguments and results.
storage_tier.title: Storage Tier

stt_redact.description: Classes the speech-to-text provider masks as it transcribes (`pci` card numbers, `pii` personal details, `phi` health details, `numbers` every number). Only providers that support it apply it; others ignore it with a validation warning.
stt_redact.title: Stt Redact

telemetry_pii.description: Whether a third-party OpenTelemetry exporter configured on the worker (an `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` endpoint) receives the conversation text and tool payloads (`LIVEKIT_TELEMETRY_ALLOW_PII`). It does not change what LiveKit Cloud Insights receives (that is the project's setting in the LiveKit Cloud dashboard). The worker applies it once per process: the first session's setting holds for later sessions that reuse the same process.
telemetry_pii.title: Telemetry Pii

PrivacyConfig.title: PrivacyConfig

ProviderRef.description: Points at a registry provider plus the credential and options to use.
ProviderRef.title: ProviderRef

ProviderRule.description: A hosted moderation service. The text trips the rule when the service flags it.

categories.description: Only these categories trip the rule; empty: any category the service flags.
categories.title: Categories

credential_id.description: The OpenAI key to use; `None` uses the agent's own OpenAI language-model key.
credential_id.title: Credential Id

provider.description: `openai_moderation`: OpenAI's moderation service (free with an OpenAI key).
provider.title: Provider

ProviderRule.title: ProviderRule

ProviderToolDefinition.description:
One action of a connected app run through a tool provider (docs/v5/COMPOSIO.md §3, D-V5-C8).

Created by materialisation (``POST /v1/tool-providers/composio/materialise``): the
parameters are pinned from the provider's schema at import, the description is its first
sentence (editable). The worker runs it with ``POST /api/v3.1/tools/execute/{tool_slug}``
on the provider's host. ``headers`` carry the provider key as a ``{{ secret.NAME }}``
placeholder that the api substitutes from ``credential_id`` when a session resolves, as
for HTTP tools; ``connection_id`` is the connected-app row, ``subject`` the provider's
``user_id`` copied from it.
ProviderToolDefinition.title: ProviderToolDefinition

PublishGate.description: Whether publishing needs a passing test run on the version being published (opt-in).

min_pass_ratio.description: The share of cases that must pass (1.0 = every case).
min_pass_ratio.title: Min Pass Ratio

require_tests.description: Refuse to publish unless the latest test run on this version passed.
require_tests.title: Require Tests

PublishGate.title: PublishGate

QaConfig.description: Post-call scoring of the session by an LLM judge.

fields.description: Post-call fields (V5-30, at most 20): the judge fills each from the finished conversation into `session_qa.raw['fields']`; they run only when QA is on.
fields.title: Fields

QaConfig.title: QaConfig

QaField.description:
One post-call field the judge fills from the finished conversation (V5-30, P §4.2 C23).

Results land in ``session_qa.raw["fields"]`` as ``{name: value}``; a value
the conversation does not state is ``null``. ``select`` takes exactly one of
``options``; the other types take no ``options``.

description.description: What the field means, in words the judge reads (e.g. 'the kind of claim the caller reports').
description.title: Description

name.description: Lowercase identifier (letters, digits, underscores); the JSON key and CSV column.
name.title: Name

options.description: The choices of a `select` field (one is picked); empty for the other types.
options.title: Options

QaField.title: QaField

QaNode.description: Post-call scoring step; never part of the conversational graph.
QaNode.title: QaNode

RecordingConfig.description: Whether and where the session is recorded through Egress.

consent_text.description: The question asked before recording when no consent block supplies one; empty uses the workspace's recording question (Settings → Compliance).
consent_text.title: Consent Text

require_consent.description: Start the recording only after the caller agrees (a tap on a consent block, or out loud); a caller who declines is never recorded.
require_consent.title: Require Consent

RecordingConfig.title: RecordingConfig

RegexRule.description: A pattern (Python regular expression syntax). The text trips the rule when it matches anywhere.

ignore_case.description: Match upper and lower case alike.
ignore_case.title: Ignore Case

pattern.description: A regular expression, e.g. `\b(?:\d[ -]?){13,19}\b` for card numbers. A pattern that does not compile, or that repeats a repeated group (slow on long text), is refused on save.
pattern.title: Pattern

RegexRule.title: RegexRule

ResolvedCompliance.description: The effective wording for one workspace: its rewrites, else its jurisdiction's preset.

disclosure_text.default: Just so you know, you're talking to an AI assistant.
disclosure_text.title: Disclosure Text

recording_text.default: This call can be recorded so we have a record of it. Is it okay if we record it?
recording_text.title: Recording Text

ResolvedCompliance.title: ResolvedCompliance

ResolvedProvider.description: A provider ready to construct: class path plus complete constructor kwargs.
ResolvedProvider.title: ResolvedProvider

Rule.description: ``when`` the condition holds, ``then`` run the actions (see the module docstring).
Rule.title: Rule

SmsTarget.description: One number ``send_sms`` may text, named by its label (V5-25).

label.description: What the model and the caller call it
label.title: Label

SmsTarget.title: SmsTarget

StartNode.description: Entry point: greets the caller and hands off along its first matching edge.
StartNode.title: StartNode

sms_targets.description: Numbers the agent may text by label, besides the caller of a phone call (send_sms).
sms_targets.title: Sms Targets

ToolBinding.description:
Copy one part of a successful tool result onto the panel or into a variable (D-V6-23).

Applied by the worker after a successful call (an HTTP 2xx, an app action that
succeeded, an MCP result that is not an error) and before the model's next turn, with
no model involved. ``path`` points into the tool's result as the model would see it
(after ``result_path``); ``""`` is the whole result.
ToolBinding.title: ToolBinding

ToolContextSpec.description: The tool-context settings of one MCP tool (``McpServerDefinition.tool_context``).
ToolContextSpec.title: ToolContextSpec

ToolExecution.description:
How one tool runs relative to the conversation (BACKGROUND-TOOLS.md §2).

The agent-level default (``ToolsConfig.execution_default``) only ever reaches read
tools: GET HTTP tools and the built-ins in :data:`BACKGROUNDABLE_BUILTINS`. The
tools in :data:`NEVER_BACKGROUND_TOOLS` and the flow edge tools always block.
ToolExecution.title: ToolExecution

ToolNode.description:
Call one of the agent's attached tools with no model turn, then branch on the outcome (D-V6-28).

The worker runs the tool the moment the step is entered — through the same execution path
as a call the model makes (blocking, the same guardrails and fences) — applies
:attr:`bindings` to the result, and takes the edge :attr:`on` names for the outcome. The
result text itself never reaches the model: what the next steps need goes into variables
(``var:<name>`` bindings), which a later step's instructions show fenced, or onto the panel.
ToolNode.title: ToolNode

ToolNodeOutcomes.description: Which outgoing edge a ``tool`` node takes for each outcome (edge ids).
ToolNodeOutcomes.title: ToolNodeOutcomes

ToolTrigger.description: After one of these tools returns (built-in, attached or block tool names).
ToolTrigger.title: ToolTrigger

ToolsConfig.description: Built-in tool gating plus references to admin-authored tool rows.

fetch_url_allowed_hosts.description: Web sites the agent may read pages from with `fetch_url`; empty, it has no `fetch_url` tool.
fetch_url_allowed_hosts.title: Fetch Url Allowed Hosts

notify_team.description: A webhook the agent posts a short summary to (`notify_team`, and escalations).

sms.description: The text-message service (an `sms` provider such as Twilio or Telnyx) and its sending number; set, the agent gets the `send_sms` tool.

web_search.description: The web search service (a `web_search` provider such as Tavily or Brave); set, the agent gets the `web_search` tool.

ToolsConfig.title: ToolsConfig

TransferNode.description: Hands the call to a human or another number.
TransferNode.title: TransferNode

TransferTarget.description: One destination the agent may transfer a caller to.

label.description: What the model and the caller call it
label.title: Label

mode.description: cold: hand the call over at once. warm: the agent calls the person first and briefs them while the caller is on hold, then joins them (LiveKit Cloud only; elsewhere the transfer is cold and the summary is kept on the call).
mode.title: Mode

TransferTarget.title: TransferTarget

TurnDetectorSettings.description:
``PipelineConfig.turn_detector``: the end-of-turn model's placement and sensitivity.

Applies to the LiveKit turn detector (``inference.TurnDetector``, 1.8.3
``inference/eot/detector.py:35-47``) and to the local plugin model, on top of the
connection's ``turn_detector_mode``: a connection without hosted Inference always
